slides.heading: Booleans
slides.body: Booleans is part of Variables and Primitive Data Types. This short lesson gives you a practical Python idea you can understand, try, and reuse in simple programs.

slides.heading: Core Idea: Booleans
slides.body: A boolean stores only one of two values: True or False. Booleans are important for decisions and conditions.

slides.heading: Real-World Analogy
slides.body: A boolean is like a light switch. It is either on or off, True or False.

slides.heading: Key Rule
slides.body: Use clear variable names and match the data type to the kind of value you need to store.

slides.heading: Try It Yourself!
slides.prompt: Create a boolean variable named is_ready with the value True and print it.
slides.hint: Remember that True starts with a capital T in Python.

quiz.prompt_text: Which of the following is a valid boolean value in Python?
quiz.explanation: Great work! In Python, boolean values are True and False — they must start with a capital letter. lowercase versions will cause an error.

quiz.prompt_text: Arrange the following lines in the correct order to create a boolean variable and print it.
quiz.explanation: First the comment describes the purpose, then the boolean is assigned, and finally print() shows whether the value is True or False.

quiz.prompt_text: Create a boolean variable named is_logged_in set to True and print it.

content.hint: Remember True starts with a capital T. Then use print(is_logged_in).

quiz.correct_answer: Any valid Python code that satisfies the prompt.
quiz.explanation: is_logged_in = True stores the boolean, and print(is_logged_in) outputs True. Booleans are perfect for on/off or yes/no states.
